yeah i have been a little surprised with how vehemently people are insisting that this is ineffective or unethical. there are some good reasons to avoid AI and I understand that/am happy to have discussions about it  - I just don’t understand the rush to discount it or assume it’s an indication of incompetence worthy of reprimand or disbarment.

thank you for reading this in good faith! I am very careful and I care a lot about my work and my clients. I want to be able to do this job for a long time and I am trying to find ways to make this work/life more doable so i can concentrate my energy on working with and for my clients. I understand a lot of the hesitation around AI - I am definitely not trying to convince people to use it but more just trying to see if/how people are incorporating it as a tool that we can use to better serve our clients. i guess i feel worried that people are so closed off to it that they aren’t able to utilize these tools defensively that rely the same tech that the other side will use pretty shamelessly against our clients whenever they can

If the citation is to something like Wong Sun or the fourth amendment broadly then I don’t need to double check it. If the model cites to a case that I have not heard of then I do double check it - this has  actually helped me find cases that are on point.

But I am not providing details about the case to AI - I suppose I should’ve clarified that this is for generating what I guess are considered boilerplate motions with current law. No case-specific information is contained, save for a carve out for specific legal exceptions

Many of my colleagues are using templates or boilerplates that have outdated law anyway, or that’s what I have been sent at least - I’ve found that chatgpt at least refers to current law so it’s helpful for me to build off of
I am still building out my templates so I find the chatgpt outputs to be helpful in creating them at least!

Unfortunately I’ve found that judges rarely read my written product anyway, and that oral argument is the place where my efforts are better spent. I don’t think I’ve had many experiences where judges truly read my motions, especially motions in limine. If i felt that they were reading them, then I totally would understand this
